41.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
41.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

42.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
42.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

43.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
43.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

44.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
44.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

45.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
45.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.

46.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
46.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
46.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

47.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
47.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: 'They were forbidden / prohibited' — said of people who were told not to do something; the passive of forbidding directed at a group.
5.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (the u-vowelling signals the passive: the subjects had the prohibition imposed on them). The long -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. The written alif after it is a spelling convention on plural verbs and is not pronounced.
5.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — to forbid, to prohibit, to restrain

6.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
6.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

7.meaning: secret talk — a confidential conversation, private consultation, or whispered exchange held quietly aside from others.
7.grammar: A feminine noun with the definite article al- ("the"), ending in a long ā written as alif maqṣūra. Because of this fixed ā ending, its case does not change in pronunciation. It denotes a hushed, private discussion.
7.root: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — to confide privately, speak in secret, draw aside

8.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
8.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

9.meaning: go back
9.grammar: A verb (present/imperfect tense). The prefix marks the subject person; the stem carries the action.

10.meaning: 'Regarding what / as to that which'. A compound joining the preposition 'to/for/regarding' with the relative pronoun 'what / that which', introducing a clause about a thing or matter.
10.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'to', 'for', or 'regarding'. 'mā' is a relative pronoun meaning 'what' or 'that which', used for things and ideas (not persons). It has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

11.meaning: 'They were forbidden / prohibited' — said of people who were told not to do something; the passive of forbidding directed at a group.
11.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (the u-vowelling signals the passive: the subjects had the prohibition imposed on them). The long -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. The written alif after it is a spelling convention on plural verbs and is not pronounced.
11.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — to forbid, to prohibit, to restrain

12.meaning: A combination meaning 'from him / from it / about him.' The preposition denotes moving away from, departing from, or concerning a thing, and the pronoun refers to a single masculine entity.
12.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. ʿan governs the genitive and conveys separation or 'concerning.' The attached -hu marks a third-person masculine singular object ('him/it').

13.grammar: A noun in context, taking the case required by its syntactic role.

14.meaning: 'In / with sin' — sin being a wrongful, blameworthy act that incurs guilt. The bi- prefix gives the sense of doing something 'by means of' or 'in the matter of' sin.
14.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, in, by') plus the definite article al- and the noun ithm. The final -i is the genitive case, which is required after the preposition bi-. The word names sinful, guilt-bearing conduct in general.

15.meaning: 'And transgression / hostile aggression' — overstepping just limits by wronging or attacking others. The leading 'and' joins it to a preceding word.
15.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and'), the article al-, and the noun ʿudwān. The -i ending is genitive; here it follows because the word is joined by 'and' to a preceding genitive noun, sharing its case. The term denotes wrongful overstepping and hostility.

16.grammar: A word form; its grammatical role is determined by its position and the case ending.

17.grammar: A noun in context, taking the case required by its syntactic role.

18.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
18.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

19.meaning: they came to you — to arrive at or approach someone. This combines the verb 'they came' with an attached 'you', i.e. they presented themselves before a single male addressee.
19.grammar: A past-tense Form I verb. The -ū ending is the masculine-plural subject ('they'), marking completed action. The attached -ka is an object pronoun, 'you' (a single male). The plural normally carries a silent trailing alif, which drops before the attached pronoun. The hamzah is the final root letter.

20.grammar: A verb form. The subject is encoded in the word through its prefix and/or suffix.

21.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
21.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

22.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

22.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

23.grammar: A verb (present/imperfect tense). The prefix marks the subject person; the stem carries the action.

24.meaning: By it, with it, through it; the preposition 'bi' (with/by means of) joined to a pronoun referring to something previously mentioned.
24.grammar: A preposition plus an attached third-person masculine singular pronoun ('it / him'). 'Bi' conveys instrument or means ('by means of it'); the pronoun takes the -i vowel because words governed by 'bi' stand in the genitive.

25.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
25.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

26.meaning: A verb meaning 'and they say / and they keep saying' — to utter or assert in speech. The structure presents an ongoing or repeated act of speaking by a group.
26.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb joined by wa- ('and'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks the 3rd-person masculine plural ('they'); the full -ūna ending is the inseparable indicative-plural suffix, showing the verb is in its base (indicative) form and expressing an ongoing or habitual action.

27.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
27.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

28.meaning: Themselves / their own selves — the noun nafs ('self, soul, person, inner being') joined to a pronoun 'their'. Used reflexively it means 'their own selves' and conveys the inmost self, the seat of desires and the person as a whole.
28.grammar: The plural noun anfus ('selves') carries the genitive -i ending followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by a preposition or joined to a preceding word; -him makes it 'their selves'.
28.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, inner being

29.meaning: A particle of urging or exhortation meaning 'why not …?' — used to press for or demand that something be done, and sometimes to express a wish, often with a tone of reproach ('why does … not happen?').
29.grammar: An indivisible particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). Although written as one form, it is not built up from the conditional 'if' plus a negation; in this prompting usage it is a single fixed particle meaning 'why not?' / 'if only.' Followed by a verb it presses for that action. (Note: in a different construction the same form can mean 'were it not for,' but that is a separate usage.) It is a particle and takes no case ending.

30.grammar: A verb (present/imperfect tense). The prefix marks the subject person; the stem carries the action.

31.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
31.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

32.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
32.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

33.meaning: A verb meaning 'we say' — the act of speaking or uttering words, in the first-person plural.
33.grammar: Present-tense verb, first-person plural ('we say'). The na- prefix means 'we'; this is a hollow verb whose middle root letter appears as a long ū (naqūlu). The final -u is the indicative ending for a plain present/future statement.

34.meaning: It/he is enough for them; it suffices them and meets their need so nothing more is required. From a noun meaning 'sufficiency, reckoning, what is enough,' carrying the sense that a thing is fully adequate as a reckoning or accounting for someone.
34.grammar: A noun in the subject (nominative) form with the -u ending, marking it as the thing being spoken about (the 'topic' or doer of being-sufficient). The attached -hum means 'them' (a group of males or mixed) and shows for whom it suffices.
34.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to reckon, count, account; sufficiency

35.meaning: Hell / Jahannam — the proper name of the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter.
35.grammar: A proper name (the name of Hell), treated as a feminine, non-fully-inflecting noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, marking it as the subject/predicate of a statement ('… is Jahannam'). Because it is a proper name of this type, it does not take the usual final '-n' (tanwīn) of ordinary nouns.

36.meaning: A verb with attached object meaning 'they will burn in it', 'they will roast in it', or 'they will be made to endure its scorching heat'. The base verb means to enter and burn in a fire and feel its blaze.
36.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third person masculine plural, with an attached object pronoun '-hā' ('it', referring to a feminine noun such as a fire). The 'ya-…-na' frame marks the plural 'they'. The '-hā' suffix is the direct object, 'it', giving 'they burn in it'.
36.root: ص-ل-ي (ṣ-l-y) — to roast, to burn, to enter and endure a fire's heat

37.meaning: 'And how wretched / evil is …!' A fixed expression of blame and condemnation — the counterpart to 'how excellent!' It declares something thoroughly bad. The leading 'fa-' adds 'so/and.'
37.grammar: A frozen verb of blame (the opposite of ni'ma, 'how excellent'). It does not conjugate normally; it stands as an exclamation declaring something utterly bad or blameworthy. The prefixed fa- ('so/and') links it to the surrounding statement.

38.meaning: Al-maṣīr — the destination, the place or state one finally comes to; the journey's end or ultimate outcome to which things return.
38.grammar: A definite noun of place/result on the pattern mafʿil, with the long ī arising from the weak root letter yāʾ (ص-ي-ر). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or what something ultimately is. The word denotes the final place or state to which one comes.
38.root: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to become, come to, end up at

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

5.meaning: you hold secret counsel
5.grammar: A verb (present/imperfect tense). The prefix marks the subject person; the stem carries the action.

6.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
6.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

7.meaning: hold secret counsel
7.grammar: A verb (present/imperfect tense). The prefix marks the subject person; the stem carries the action.

8.meaning: 'In / with sin' — sin being a wrongful, blameworthy act that incurs guilt. The bi- prefix gives the sense of doing something 'by means of' or 'in the matter of' sin.
8.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, in, by') plus the definite article al- and the noun ithm. The final -i is the genitive case, which is required after the preposition bi-. The word names sinful, guilt-bearing conduct in general.

9.meaning: 'And transgression / hostile aggression' — overstepping just limits by wronging or attacking others. The leading 'and' joins it to a preceding word.
9.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and'), the article al-, and the noun ʿudwān. The -i ending is genitive; here it follows because the word is joined by 'and' to a preceding genitive noun, sharing its case. The term denotes wrongful overstepping and hostility.

10.meaning: and disobedience
10.grammar: A word form; its grammatical role is determined by its position and the case ending.

11.meaning: the Messenger — one sent with a message; specifically an envoy commissioned by Allah to convey His revelation. 'Rasūl' is a faʿūl-pattern noun denoting the one who is sent.
11.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') is assimilated into the 'sun letter' r (so it sounds ar-r). The ending -i marks the genitive case, the form a word typically takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
11.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message, an envoy

12.grammar: A word form; its grammatical role is determined by its position and the case ending.

13.meaning: Piety, righteousness, dutiful goodness — godly virtue expressed in genuine right action and kindness, not mere outward show.
13.grammar: The prefix 'bi-' is a preposition meaning 'with/by/to.' The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which is the form a noun takes after a preposition; it can also link the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.

14.grammar: A word form; its grammatical role is determined by its position and the case ending.

15.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'guard yourselves / be mindful and on your guard.' The verb conveys taqwā — protecting oneself by being conscious of Allah and shielding oneself from wrongdoing and its consequences.
15.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you (all).' The -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressees ('you all'). The pattern (form VIII, from waqā 'to protect') gives the sense of taking protective care for oneself.
15.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
16.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

17.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
17.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

18.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
18.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

19.meaning: 'You all will be gathered / assembled / mustered' — to be brought together into one place, as a crowd is rounded up. The root is strongly associated with the gathering of all people for the Day of Resurrection.
19.grammar: A present/future-tense passive verb ('to be gathered'). The tu-…-ūna frame marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all') as the ones acted upon, with the action ongoing or yet to come. The retained final -na indicates the verb is in its base (indicative) state.

1.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
1.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

2.meaning: secret talk — a confidential conversation, private consultation, or whispered exchange held quietly aside from others.
2.grammar: A feminine noun with the definite article al- ("the"), ending in a long ā written as alif maqṣūra. Because of this fixed ā ending, its case does not change in pronunciation. It denotes a hushed, private discussion.
2.root: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — to confide privately, speak in secret, draw aside

3.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

4.meaning: The Shayṭān — Satan, the devil: a rebellious, evil being who tempts and misleads; the term suggests one who is far removed from goodness and burning in defiance.
4.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the Satan / the devil'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
4.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote (from good/mercy); a devil

5.meaning: that he may grieve
5.grammar: A word form; its grammatical role is determined by its position and the case ending.

6.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
6.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
7.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

8.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not.' It denies that something is currently the case, functioning to negate a statement in the present, and it inflects for person like a verb.
8.grammar: A hollow negating verb fixed in form for the third-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'); the -a ending belongs to its frozen past-tense shape. Though past in form, it negates in the present. It introduces a subject and a predicate, denying the link between them. The prefix wa means 'and'.

9.meaning: he (can) harm them
9.grammar: A verb form. The subject is encoded in the word through its prefix and/or suffix.

10.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
10.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

11.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
11.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

12.meaning: 'By the leave of / with the permission of' — formed from 'with/by' plus 'permission, leave, sanction'. It conveys that something happens by someone's authorization or enabling will.
12.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition 'with/by'. The noun 'idhn' means 'permission, leave, sanction'. After the preposition it takes the genitive -i ending, the form used following a preposition and typically linking on to a following noun ('the permission OF …').
12.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; also listening/ear

13.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
13.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

14.meaning: A two-part phrase: the joining word 'and' plus the preposition 'on / upon / incumbent upon,' often used to express an obligation resting on someone.

4.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.

5.meaning: 'It was said' — speech was uttered or a statement was made. The passive form: the saying is reported without naming who spoke.

The lām is the third root letter, not an ending; the final -a is simply the default short vowel of the third-person masculine singular past, here used impersonally as 'it was said'.

22.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
22.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.

23.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
23.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

24.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
24.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
24.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

25.meaning: Knowledge — sure, established awareness and understanding of how things truly are, as opposed to ignorance, guesswork, or mere opinion.
25.grammar: A definite noun ('the knowledge'). The -a ending marks the accusative case, which most often signals that the noun is the direct object of a verb (the thing being received or acted upon) or otherwise governed into that case.
25.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge, sure awareness

26.meaning: "degrees / ranks / levels / steps" — the plural of daraja, a step or grade in an ascending scale; it denotes ranks, levels, or stages of elevation.
26.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks sound feminine plural). The final -in (with nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('degrees, ranks') and in the accusative/genitive case — the form used as an object or after a preposition.
26.root: د-ر-ج (d-r-j) — step, grade, to ascend by degrees

27.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
27.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
27.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

28.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
28.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

29.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
29.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
29.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

30.meaning: 'Fully aware / All-Aware' — one who knows the inner reality and hidden details of things through intimate, expert knowledge. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect awareness of all that is concealed.
30.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, thorough quality ('thoroughly aware'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative (tanwīn ḍamm): it marks an indefinite noun/adjective in the nominative case, the form used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.

7.grammar: A noun in context, taking the case required by its syntactic role.

8.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

9.meaning: The two hands; figuratively "front, presence, fore-part." In the phrase "between the two hands of" it idiomatically means "in front of, ahead of, in advance of."
9.grammar: A dual noun ("two hands") in its connected form. The -ay ending is the dual in the genitive/accusative state and signals that it is linked to a following noun ("the two hands OF …"); the final -n of the dual drops because it is joined to what follows.

10.grammar: A verb (present/imperfect tense). The prefix marks the subject person; the stem carries the action.

11.meaning: A charity / alms — a freely given gift to the needy, given to seek Allah's pleasure and confirm one's sincerity; it can also denote the obligatory alms (zakāt). Stated indefinitely, 'a charity'.
11.grammar: A feminine noun, 'charity/alms'. The ending -tan combines the feminine marker (tā' marbūṭa) with nunation: it marks the word as indefinite ('a charity') and accusative — the form used for the object of a verb.
11.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity; charitable giving that confirms it

12.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
12.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

13.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
13.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
13.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

14.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
14.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

15.meaning: And purer / cleaner — freer from defilement and impurity, more cleansed in both the physical and moral sense.
15.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus a comparative adjective ('purer'), on the pattern 'afʿal formed by the a- prefix. The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

16.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
16.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

17.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
17.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

18.meaning: You (all) find, come upon, or obtain something. The verb covers both locating something searched for and finding oneself in a state or circumstance.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ū ending makes it plural ('you all'). The shortened spelling (dropping the final nūn) shows it is in the jussive/subjunctive mood, the form used after particles like 'lam' (did not) or 'not'.
18.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to obtain, to find oneself in a state

19.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
19.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

20.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
20.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

21.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
21.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.

22.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
22.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

14.meaning: Then establish / set up and keep up — to make something stand firm and perform it fully and properly (classically used of duly observing prayer); a command to a group.
14.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural ('you all establish'). It is a 'form IV' verb (the a- shaping gives the causative sense 'make it stand / keep it up'). The -ū ending directs the order to a group. The leading fa- is a connecting particle ('then, so').
14.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, establish, set upright

15.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
15.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

16.meaning: And give / hand over / bring — a command to deliver something to someone, to render it to its due recipient.

17.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure; to grow, increase, be blessed

18.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a masculine plural ('you all obey!'), joined by 'wa' ('and'). The '-ū' ending marks the plural addressee in commands.
18.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, comply, submit willingly

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
19.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

20.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
20.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.

21.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
21.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
21.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

22.meaning: 'Fully aware / All-Aware' — one who knows the inner reality and hidden details of things through intimate, expert knowledge. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect awareness of all that is concealed.
22.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, thorough quality ('thoroughly aware'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative (tanwīn ḍamm): it marks an indefinite noun/adjective in the nominative case, the form used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.

23.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
23.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

24.meaning: You (plural) do, make, work, or act. A present/future verb addressed to a group, covering deeds and actions in general — what people carry out and put into practice.
24.grammar: Present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'); the -ūna ending makes it masculine plural ('you all') and signals the indicative mood — the ordinary statement-form used for actions that are happening or will happen. Within -ūna the long ū (wāw) carries the plurality and the final n (nūn) marks the indicative.

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: 'They turned away / they turned their backs / they turned aside'. It conveys turning oneself away from something, often implying rejection or withdrawal.
5.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine plural: the ending '-aw' means 'they (did) …'. The Form V pattern (with the 'ta-' prefix and doubled middle letter) gives a reflexive sense — turning oneself away. It states a completed act.
5.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near/turn toward; in this form, to turn away

6.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
6.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

7.meaning: wrath
7.grammar: A word form; its grammatical role is determined by its position and the case ending.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
9.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
9.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
10.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

11.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
11.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

12.meaning: 'From you / among you (plural)' — indicating a part taken out of, or belonging to, a group of people being addressed.
12.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun -kum ('you all,' masculine plural). Together they express partition or origin: a part drawn 'from / among' the addressed group.

13.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

14.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
14.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

15.meaning: 'And they swear' — the conjunction 'and' with a verb meaning to take an oath, to vow solemnly that something is true.
15.grammar: The wa- means 'and'. The verb is present-tense: the ya- prefix marks third-person, the long -ū carries the masculine plural subject 'they', and the final -na is the indicative marker for a plain ongoing or habitual action. The verb means to bind oneself by a solemn oath.
15.root: ح-ل-ف (ḥ-l-f) — to swear, take an oath

16.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
16.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
16.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

17.grammar: A noun in context, taking the case required by its syntactic role.

18.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
18.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

19.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
19.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

1.meaning: He has prepared / made ready — to set something up in advance, to ready or get it in order beforehand.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he prepared'). It belongs to the 'form IV' pattern (the a- prefix gives the sense of actively making something ready). With no added subject suffix, the bare form means 'he' did the action, completed in the past. The doubled middle letter (shadda) is part of this root.
1.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — to count, prepare, make ready

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

4.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
4.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

5.meaning: 'Severe / intense / harsh.' An adjective describing something strong, forceful, and hard to bear.
5.grammar: An adjective in an intensive pattern ('very strong/severe'). The -an ending marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the form used when it describes a noun that is itself indefinite and accusative.
5.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, severe

6.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
6.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

7.meaning: 'It was evil / how evil it is' — a past-tense verb of blame expressing that something is bad, wretched, or wicked. As a verb of dispraise it conveys strong condemnation of a thing.
7.grammar: A Form I past-tense (perfect) verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he/it'). The final -a is not a separate grammatical ending: it is the third root letter (the hamza, ء) carrying its default fatḥa in the 3rd-person masculine singular perfect. As a frozen verb of blame it functions much like 'how evil is …!'
7.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, evil, to grieve or distress

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
9.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

10.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
10.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
10.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: They took for themselves, adopted, acquired, or chose something. From a verb meaning to take or seize. The reflexive Form VIII shape adds the sense of taking for one's own benefit or making something into something.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the reflexive (Form VIII) pattern, third-person masculine plural: 'they took for themselves / adopted.' The -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') in the past tense. The initial helping vowel i- and the doubled t belong to the Form VIII shape, which often gives the verb a self-directed sense ('to take for oneself').

2.meaning: Their oaths / solemn sworn pledges. The noun denotes binding declarations sworn to affirm a commitment.
2.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -hum suffix means 'their' (referring to a masculine or mixed group). The -a vowel before the suffix reflects the accusative case, which typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
2.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand; by extension, oath, good fortune

3.meaning: (as) a cover
3.grammar: A noun in context, taking the case required by its syntactic role.

4.meaning: The compound 'and they barred / turned away / hindered' — the connector 'and/so' joined to a past-tense verb meaning to turn (people) away, block, obstruct, or divert them from a path or purpose, referring to a group of males. The root expresses both turning oneself away and turning others back.
4.grammar: The connective 'so/then' (fa-) prefixed to a past-tense (perfect) verb. The ending -ū marks 'they', a group of males (third-person masculine plural). The doubled middle consonant (ṣadd-) reflects the geminate root. The fa- links this action as a consequence or sequel to what precedes.
4.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to turn away, bar, obstruct

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

5.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

6.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
6.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: "So for them / then theirs is" — a combination meaning 'then/so, belonging to them'. It introduces a consequence ('so') and asserts that something is for or owed to a group ('for them').
8.grammar: A connective 'fa' ('so, then', often marking a result) plus the preposition 'la' ('for, belonging to') plus the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them', masculine plural). Together they express possession or entitlement following from what preceded.

9.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
9.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

10.meaning: 'Humiliating / disgracing / degrading' — an active participle describing something that brings abasement and disgrace upon its object.
10.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word, like '-ing' in English) from the causative (form IV) pattern, meaning 'one that causes humiliation.' The -un ending (indefinite nominative tanwīn) marks an indefinite noun in the nominative case — the case of a subject or, commonly, of something described as existing ('a humiliating [thing]').
10.root: ه-و-ن (h-w-n) — being lowly, easy, contemptible; hence humiliation

1.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
1.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.

2.meaning: To avail / to be of use / to ward off need; from a verb meaning to enrich or make independent, hence 'to be of any benefit' or 'to suffice (someone) against' a threat — typically used to deny that something can help at all.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a on the stem-vowel (-iya). The tu- prefix marks the doer as 'it/she' (third-person feminine singular) or a second-person 'you'. The subjunctive typically appears after particles meaning 'that', 'so that', or 'will not', expressing a non-factual, hoped-for, or negated action rather than a plain statement.
2.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, self-sufficient; hence to avail/suffice

3.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
3.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

4.meaning: Their wealth / their possessions. The base noun amwāl is the plural of māl, meaning property, wealth, goods, or money — anything owned of value. With the attached pronoun it means 'their wealth'.
4.grammar: A plural noun with the -u (nominative) ending, which generally marks it as the subject of a sentence or a predicate. The attached pronoun -hum means 'their' (a group, grammatically masculine plural) when joined to a noun.
4.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — wealth, property, to be wealthy

5.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

6.meaning: Their children / their offspring. The base noun awlād is the plural of walad, meaning a child or offspring (son or, broadly, descendant). With the attached pronoun it means 'their children'.
6.grammar: A plural noun with the -u (nominative) ending, generally marking it as a subject or predicate. The attached pronoun -hum means 'their' (a group, grammatically masculine plural) when joined to a noun.
6.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; hence child, offspring

7.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
7.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

8.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
8.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

9.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
9.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

10.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
10.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

11.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
11.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

12.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
12.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

13.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
13.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

14.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
14.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

15.meaning: 'Ones who abide / remain forever; everlasting dwellers.' The plural of an active participle describing those who stay, persist, and endure in a state or place without end — abiding permanently.
15.grammar: An active participle in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when such a group is the subject of a sentence or is being described as being in that state.
15.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — to remain forever, endure, be everlasting

1.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
1.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

2.meaning: A finite present/future verb meaning 'He raises them / brings them back to life / sends them forth' — to resurrect or dispatch, joined with 'them' as those acted upon.
2.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('He'). The ya- prefix marks that subject. The attached -hum ('them') is the object raised; the final -u here is a helping vowel added so that '-hum' joins smoothly to a following word. The base sense covers both raising the dead and sending someone forth on a mission.
2.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to raise up, resurrect, send forth

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
4.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

5.meaning: then they will swear
5.grammar: A noun in context, taking the case required by its syntactic role.

6.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
6.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

7.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
7.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

8.meaning: They swear, take an oath, or vow — to make a solemn declaration, often invoking Allah's name as a pledge.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix plus -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The full -ūna ending (nūn intact) signals the indicative mood — a plain statement of ongoing action.
8.root: ح-ل-ف (ḥ-l-f) — to swear, take an oath

The full -ūna ending (indicative mood) presents the action as ongoing or habitual fact: 'they (do) believe.'

40.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

41.meaning: 'And they were pleased / and they were content' — the act of being satisfied and approving, here done by a group. Joins a connecting 'and' to a past-tense verb whose ending marks a plural 'they' as the ones who became pleased.
41.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus a past-tense (perfect) verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), presenting the action as completed: 'they were/became pleased.' The trailing alif is a silent spelling convention after this plural ending, not pronounced.
41.root: ر-ض-و / ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-w/y) — to be pleased, content, approving

42.meaning: A combination meaning 'from him / from it / about him.' The preposition denotes moving away from, departing from, or concerning a thing, and the pronoun refers to a single masculine entity.
42.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. ʿan governs the genitive and conveys separation or 'concerning.' The attached -hu marks a third-person masculine singular object ('him/it').

43.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
43.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

44.grammar: A noun in context, taking the case required by its syntactic role.

45.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
45.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

46.meaning: An opening particle of alert and emphasis — 'Now then!', 'Beware!', 'Truly!'. It calls attention to and strongly affirms the statement that follows.
46.grammar: An attention-drawing particle placed at the start of a statement. It rouses the listener and emphasizes what comes next, somewhat like 'Indeed!', 'Lo!', or 'Take note!' in English.

47.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
47.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

48.meaning: "Party / faction / band," the noun "ḥizb" denoting a group, company, or partisan body of people united by a common cause or allegiance.
48.grammar: This is a singular noun. The final "-a" ending is the accusative case, taken by a noun when it is the direct object of a verb or the first term ("the party of …") of a possessive pairing with a following noun.
48.root: ح-ز-ب (ḥ-z-b) — a group, party, or faction; a band of people

49.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
49.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

50.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
50.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

51.meaning: The successful ones / those who prosper and attain — people who achieve genuine, lasting success: they win what they seek, are saved from what they fear, and flourish. The term implies thriving and triumph, not merely worldly gain.
51.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action, from the fourth verb form 'afʿala) meaning 'one who attains success', with the definite article 'the'. The plural ending -ūna marks a masculine plural in the nominative case, which typically signals the subject (the doer) of a sentence.
51.root: ف-ل-ح (f-l-ḥ) — to prosper, succeed, attain, flourish
